title: Positions: Above, Below, Next To, In Front Of, Behind
seo_title: Kindergarten Position Words Worksheets: Above, Below, Beside, In Front Of, Behind
standard_text: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten position words worksheets: above, below, next to, between, in front of and behind with tables, shelves, boxes and shapes. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Position words tell where things are: above, below, next to, in front of, behind.
key_sub: If the ball is above the table, the table is below the ball.
body_html:
Position words tell where things are

WordMeaning
abovehigher than
belowlower than, under
next to / besideat the side of
betweenin the middle of two things
in front ofcloser to you
behindfarther away, partly hidden

Above and below

In front of and behind

If something covers part of the box, it is in front of the box. If the box covers part of it, it is behind the box.

Turn it around

If the ball is above the table, then the table is below the ball.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Mixing up above and belowAbove is up high. Below is down low
Mixing up in front of and behindAsk: what is hiding part of what?
Saying next to for the middle thingUse between when it has a thing on each side

faq.q: Which position words do kindergartners learn?
faq.a: Above, below, beside, next to, in front of and behind. Many classes also use between, top, middle and bottom.

faq.q: Why are position words part of math?
faq.a: They help children describe shapes and space. Later they use the same ideas for maps, graphs and geometry.

faq.q: How can I practice position words at home?
faq.a: Play hide and seek with a toy and ask: Is it under the table? Behind the chair? Give directions like 'Put the cup next to the plate'.

faq.q: My child mixes up in front of and behind. What helps?
faq.a: Stand a toy and a box on a table. Move the toy and ask which one hides part of the other. The one that is hidden is behind.
